anomalies.observed: Both ground pins of each isolated CAN transceiver are connected to the common GND net: U1 pin 4 (GND1) and pin 5 (GND2), and U40 pin 4 (GND1) and pin 5 (GND2).
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 (logic side) and GND2 (bus side) should be separate isolated grounds. Tying GND2 to the main GND defeats the intended galvanic isolation of the CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN buses are not isolated as intended; the bus-side ground is tied to the CM4/main ground, allowing ground loops and removing the isolation barrier.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of D26, D40, and D47 are connected only to each other on net /NET0003; there is no connection from that net to +3V3 or any other supply/current source.
anomalies.expected: Status LEDs whose cathodes are tied through current-limit resistors to active-low driver outputs should have their common anodes connected to the appropriate supply rail (here +3V3) so current can flow when the driver sinks.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet/activity LEDs connected to this common-anode net cannot light because their anodes are floating.

anomalies.observed: CM4 pin 92 (RUN_PG) is connected only to U27 pin 2 (A). There is no pull-up resistor on this net.
anomalies.expected: RUN_PG is an open-drain output and should be pulled up to a defined logic high before driving a buffer input; otherwise the connected buffer input can float.
anomalies.impact: The U27 input can float, making the RUN_PG-derived power-enable/switch path unpredictable and potentially contributing to inconsistent CM4 power-on behavior.

parsed.summary: The design files contain at least one high-confidence anomaly: the isolated CAN transceivers have both their primary and secondary grounds tied to common GND, defeating the intended CAN isolation. Secondary connectivity issues also appear: several status LED anodes are left floating, and the CM4 RUN_PG open-drain output lacks a pull-up before driving a buffer input.
